brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: vertical stack piece:0,0,0;full (level 0) + snap:0,0,0;full + piece:0,0,1;full (level1) + snap:0,0,1;full + piece:0,0,2;full (level2) = 3 levels at same q,r
drawer:0#0,1#cut on cut face of piece:0,1,0;half-n at level 0, and notch:0#-1,1#notch1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) in notch between piece:-1,0,0;full and piece:0,0,0;full – both at level 0

requirements.requirement: open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full (hex-bin-full open tray) at q0 r0 level2 – top storey

finish.summary: Built 3-high tower at 0,0 (levels 0-2). Bottom level has two drawer storages: a cut-face drawer on half-n at 0,1,0 and a notch drawer frame at -1,1,0. Top level has open bin hex-bin-full at 0,0,2. Joint bolts lock bottom bodies; meshClash clear, no errors.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
